I’m a senior and I’ve got two exams, a group project (where I’m basically the project manager by default), and I’m also trying to finish internship applications. Everyone keeps saying “just take breaks,” but I don’t really have the luxury of falling behind. At home it’s… not exactly acceptable to struggle, so I’m trying to handle this quietly and not make a scene.

Could you help me set up a realistic study plan for the next 10 days? Like a time-blocked schedule I can actually follow, including when to do practice problems vs. review notes, and how to structure breaks so they don’t turn into me losing an entire evening.

Also, I’m on a tight budget and mostly eating on campus (food court / dining hall). I’m trying to keep it “clean” and not feel sluggish, but I don’t want to spend extra money. What are a few default meals/snacks I can rely on that are quick and won’t wreck my focus?

And last thing (sorry): my sleep is completely flipped. I keep telling myself I’ll go to bed earlier, then it’s 3am and I’m still staring at Anki cards. If you have any sleep + focus hacks for finals week that don’t involve counseling appointments or anything time-intensive, I’d really appreciate it.

Hey AS, I’m glad you reached out. Finals week sounds incredibly overwhelming with everything on your plate, and it’s okay to feel like you’re spiraling. Let’s tackle one thing at a time to help you regain some control.

For a realistic 10-day study plan, start by blocking your day into chunks: 3-4 hours of focused study in the morning (e.g., 8-12), split between practice problems (2 hours) and note review (1-2 hours). Afternoon can be for group project tasks (1-2 hours). Reserve evenings for lighter review or internship apps (2 hours max). Build in 15-30 minute breaks every 2 hours—set a timer to avoid losing track. Cap your day by 10 PM to protect sleep.

On food, stick to dining hall basics: opt for grilled proteins, veggies, and whole grains like rice or quinoa to stay energized. Grab fruit or yogurt for snacks—cheap and quick. Avoid heavy, greasy options that might drag you down.

For sleep, try a hard cutoff: no screens after 9:30 PM. Wind down with a quick stretch or deep breathing for 5 minutes. Keep a consistent bedtime, even if it’s late at first—aim to shift it earlier by 30 minutes each night. I’m here if you need more support.

The schedule idea you gave me helped a little (at least it sounds rational on paper). I’m trying to follow it, but I keep getting this anxious feeling that if I stop—even for a “timer break”—I’m going to lose momentum and then I’ll be behind and it’ll snowball. I feel like if I don’t control this part, I’ll show up at home after finals and get the usual comments, and I really don’t have the bandwidth for that right now.
